forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline per original question framing) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38→0.15. As of May 17, approximately 2 vessels per day transited the Strait — roughly 2% of the pre-crisis ~95/day observed baseline (USNI News, Windward AI). Note: the question's ~120/day figure is the pre-war cited baseline; USNI/Bloomberg/Windward record ~95/day as the observed pre-crisis baseline. All major Western carriers (Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd) remain suspended; 6 P&I clubs have withdrawn cover. War-risk premiums at approximately 8× pre-crisis rates (Lloyd's List, Albany Antree, 6 May), far above the 1.5% indicator threshold. A 14-point US–Iran MOU framework is under active negotiation, with Trump stating 'largely negotiated' on May 23 (NPR) and Axios publishing the 60-day framework terms on May 24. However, no deal has been signed as of May 26; Iran's FM Araghchi cited a 'deadlock' on enriched uranium removal (Times of Israel); FM spokesman Baghaei stated a signing is 'not imminent' (PressTV, 23 May); and US forces conducted 'self-defense strikes' on Iranian missile sites and mine-laying boats near Bandar Abbas on May 25 (NBC, CNBC, Washington Post) — on the same day as Doha talks — striking the very vessels whose clearance is required for Hormuz reopening. Reaching 50+ vessels per day within 15 days requires a signed MOU, ceasefire reinforcement, Iranian cooperation on mine-clearance, carrier return decisions, and insurance market reset — all serially dependent. The 0.15 reflects the non-trivial but low-probability fast-track scenario; Källa B's mine-clearing timeline concern provided a marginal upward nudge from 0.14.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime (announced May 18) count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing. Baseline note (Judge, 2026-05-26): the question's ~120/day figure is the self-cited pre-war baseline; the source-authoritative observed pre-crisis baseline per USNI News and Bloomberg is ~95/day. Resolution threshold (50 vessels/day) is anchored to the question text's 50%×120/day = 60 vessels/day floor; this is not changed mid-forecast to avoid retroactive alteration of the YES/NO outcome.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on commercial transit.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement — weekly cadence; next review Sunday. NOTE for Sunday review: The Knesset passed a preliminary (first) reading of a COALITION-SPONSORED dissolution bill 110-0 on May 20 (Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, Haaretz). This is a coalition-managed process designed to control election timing, not a loss of majority. The coalition retains 61+ seats. The bill delegates election date-setting to the House Committee after final (third) reading enactment. Netanyahu targets October 2026; Haredi parties push September 2026. Smotrich remains inside the coalition with no formal departure announced. The 110-0 vote is a controlled mechanism, not a crisis signal. Full evaluation deferred to Sunday per Codex DA #12.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party (e.g. Smotrich) departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. PATCH (Judge, 2026-05-26): If the coalition itself sponsors and passes a dissolution bill while retaining 61+ seats throughout the process, this does NOT satisfy the 'loss of 61-seat majority' YES criterion — coalition-controlled dissolution without majority loss resolves NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25→0.20. Three genuinely new downward-pressure events since May 19: (1) US conducted 'self-defense strikes' on Iranian missile sites and mine-laying boats near Bandar Abbas on May 25 (NBC, CNBC, Washington Post), concurrent with Iranian negotiators Ghalibaf and Araghchi arriving in Doha for Qatari-mediated talks — the simultaneous military strike and diplomatic engagement reflects a structural contradiction that damages Iranian domestic political space for signing. (2) Iran's FM Araghchi told reporters talks hit a 'deadlock' on enriched uranium removal, with the issue 'postponed' to later stages (Times of Israel); this is not a generic 'complex negotiation' characterisation but a named impasse on a specific core issue. (3) Iran's FM spokesman Baghaei explicitly stated that 'no one can claim that the signing of an agreement is imminent' (PressTV, 23 May). Countervailing upward pressure: Trump stated deal 'largely negotiated' (NPR, 23 May); Axios published the full 60-day MOU framework terms (24 May); both sides dispatched senior delegations to Doha (25 May). Austria intelligence assessment (May 26) that Iran pursues active nuclear weapons capability creates additional political friction but is standard IRIB-rejected boilerplate in its effect on Iranian red lines. Judge calibration: Källa A's 0.18 overstates the downward case given Trump's public commitment; Källa B's 'hold at 0.25' preceded the three new events above. Intermediate position 0.20 accepted.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Iran's Supreme Leader or acting sovereign authority disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. PATCH (Judge, 2026-05-26): removed named reference to 'Khamenei' and replaced with 'Iran's Supreme Leader or acting sovereign authority' to avoid principal-identification void if the named individual is deceased or incapacitated.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved NO. Resolution criteria not met as of EOD 2026-05-22. US State Dept announced 45-day extension May 15 and scheduled next talks for June 2-3 (Washington); Lebanon welcomed the extension. IDF/Hezbollah exchanges continued, including Israeli strikes killing 6 paramedics on May 22 (Reuters, AP, Times of Israel), but intensity remained sub-threshold — no sustained exchange at pre-April-16 levels, no >50 launches/day from either side. IDF Chief Zamir stated 'there is no ceasefire' to troops in southern Lebanon (Times of Israel), but this is a military characterisation to troops in the field, not an official US or Lebanese government declaration of void per the resolution criteria. Both governments reaffirmed the framework operative. Netanyahu ordered escalation against Hezbollah on May 25, but this occurred after the May 22 resolution horizon. Resolution: NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22→0.06. The dissolution process is formally in motion but a formal Netanyahu announcement of an early election date before June 1 is procedurally impossible on the current legislative track. The Knesset passed a preliminary (first) reading of a coalition-sponsored dissolution bill 110-0 on May 20 (Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, Haaretz). A dissolution bill requires three readings before enactment; the second and third readings are not scheduled before June 1. Following enactment, date-setting is delegated to the Knesset House Committee — an additional procedural step that further defers formal announcement. Netanyahu is targeting an October 2026 election to maximise war-credit campaigning; Haredi parties push September 2026. Neither timeline is compatible with a formal announcement before June 1. Residual 6% covers a political shock scenario (unexpected coalition fracture, emergency session, Netanyahu unilateral announcement) that is real but remote. The 110-0 vote is a signal of direction, not pace.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes the FINAL (third) reading of a formal dissolution bill by majority vote. Preliminary or second readings do NOT resolve YES. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record (specifying which reading). Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a FINAL (third) reading dissolution vote counts. PATCH (Judge, 2026-05-26): 'Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion' in resolution criteria is clarified to mean the final (third) reading of a dissolution bill. The May 20 preliminary (first) reading 110-0 vote does NOT trigger YES.
